****Job Description:

****Are you ready to drive change, foster a culture of commercial excellence, and lead strategic transformation projects? As the Regional Perfo & Transformation Manager at Satair, you will act as the primary representative for the Commercial Process, Performance & Transformation (ASCX) team in your region. You will bridge the gap between regional teams and the central ASCX pillars of processes, performance, data analytics, and automation to support Satair's commercial objectives. We are looking for a structured, results-oriented leader who can influence without authority and advocate for the region's needs within a complex, shared Airbus ecosystem.

**What The Job Is

**You will report to the Head of Commercial Data Analytics (HO ASCXY) and integrate into a multi-disciplinary team spread across the globe. In this role, you will serve as the regional node for a centralized cross-functional team, meaning you will not have direct reports but will lead by influence across regional commercial teams, account directors, and operations.

Your main responsibilities:

• Regional Commercial Project Portfolio Leadership: Accountable for the regional commercial project portfolio's financial impact and performance metrics, leading transformation projects using LBIP and Agile methodologies.

• Regional AOS Roadmap Execution: Take accountability for the successful implementation of the AOS (Airbus Operating System) regional roadmap in alignment with ASCX and the Regional Managing Director.

• Regional Representation & Connectivity: Act as a critical connector between regional teams and ASCX, representing ASCX in the Regional Customer Satisfaction Review Board (R-CSRB) and other commercial forums.

• Culture & Continuous Improvement: Proactively drive a culture of creativity, commercial excellence, and continuous improvement by identifying and addressing systemic "irritants".

Travel days to be expected are approximately 30% (domestic and international).

**How You Will Contribute To The Team

**We are looking for a proactive professional with an excellent problem-solving mindset and an ability to translate data into actionable insights. You must possess a keen understanding of business issues, key stakeholders, and external dynamics which inform priority setting.

You must hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related field, accompanied by 5-10 years of proven experience leading cross-functional, regional, and global continuous improvement and transformation projects in a complex setting. A strong understanding of aviation aftermarket commercial operations is highly preferred, as are additional certifications in process improvement methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma, Lean). You will thrive in this role if you possess a high degree of agility in learning, exceptional communication and presentation abilities, and a proactive "can-do attitude". Because you will be networking globally, an excellent command of both written and spoken English is required, while proficiency in a secondary language relevant to the assigned region is preferred.

**What does your next challenge look like?

**At SATAIR, we believe in sustainable aviation that allows people to travel and connect across the globe.

We are on a mission to provide world class material solutions that keep aircraft flying and extend their lifespan.

In Satair, you can challenge the status quo, pioneer new ways of working, and generate real value for airlines and suppliers worldwide.

Being part of the Airbus family gives us the opportunity to live a global mindset, working in international and diverse teams and collaborating across functions, sites and cultures.

If you want to work as one team embracing a can-do attitude in a demanding environment, then we offer a great place to explore, learn, and grow, making an impact on aviation’s digital and sustainable transformation.

Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company!

**About SATAIR

**Satair is an Airbus Services company offering first-class material management solutions in the aviation aftermarket industry. We take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience around the clock, driving innovation, and contributing to aviation’s digital and sustainable transformation.

With our global functional organisation spanning 12 sites and locations worldwide, and a team of over 2,000 people supporting a $3.9 billion turnover, you will be part of a truly global company that continues to grow year after year.

Welcome to the Satair family!

If you want to know more about our business, have a closer look at our website www.SATAIR.com or check out our SATAIR Youtube Channel at www.youtube.com/sataircompany !

**What do we offer at SATAIR?

**At SATAIR, you will find much more than a job - we offer you the possibility of growing both your personal and professional capacities in a fun, supportive and informal working environment, where you will be encouraged to engage, share knowledge and ideas.

SATAIR is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We love to bring in people with different backgrounds and experiences as we believe it enhances our performance immensely!

Here is a selection of some of the benefits we offer our employees in Copenhagen:

Financial Benefits: Competitive salary, Employee Stock Ownership Program, Success sharing, Health insurance, Group accident insurance, Employee discounts to local businesses

Employee Health and Wellbeing: On-site gym, App-based health & wellbeing platform, Amazing canteen at a subsided price, Massage scheme

Learning and Development: Airbus Leadership University, Large number of e-learning and training offers for personal and professional development, Promotion of professional development (e.g. postgraduate studies, technician training), Possibility of mentoring, Gain international experience

Work-life blend and life phase support: Possibility to work remotely, 4 care days, Senior days, Working from home policy (2 days remote per week)

**Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company

**Please send us your application as soon as possible to get the opportunity to become part of an exceptional global team!

We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

When applying for the position, you accept our data privacy statement: http://www.SATAIR.com/privacy

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth.

jobs.occupation: Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

**You Have

**

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

**In Practice, You Will

**

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Uffe Holme ufho@novonordisk.com

jobs.occupation: Global Reward Specialist - Job Architecture, Compensation & Pay Transparency
jobs.description:
Do you enjoy working with the structures behind fair and competitive pay? And would you like to take ownership of how job architecture, salary structures and Reward practices work across countries and entities?

This is your opportunity to take ownership of key Reward frameworks and help us mature how we work with Reward across ABENA.

As our new Global Reward Specialist, you will take ownership of key areas of our global Reward approach across countries and entities, from job architecture, salary structures and benchmarking to pay equity and Pay Transparency.

It is a role for someone who enjoys both the detail and the bigger picture: working hands-on with Reward data and frameworks while helping HR and leaders make consistent, well-informed decisions and building robust business processes.

And you will not be starting from a blank page. Important foundations are already in place. Your role is to take them further: strengthen our Reward framework, mature our approach to Pay Transparency, and turn structures and data into robust global reward practices that support consistent and well-informed decisions across ABENA.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Own and further develop ABENA’s reward framework, including pay policy, salary and bonus structures, pay ranges and related governance.

• Own and continuously improve our global job architecture, ensuring consistent job evaluation, levels and career paths across the organization.

• Drive and mature our Pay Transparency efforts, including pay equity analyses, pay-gap reporting, related governance and long-term compliance.

• Lead relevant recurring reward processes such as annual salary reviews and compensation analyses.

• Turn reward data into clear recommendations supporting pay decisions, internal equity and competitiveness.

• Advise HR and leaders on reward decisions, job leveling, promotions, new roles and organizational changes.

• Develop communication, training and guidance materials that strengthen reward capabilities and ensure consistent understanding and application of reward principles across ABENA.

What we are looking for

• A proven track record working within Reward, Compensation & Benefits, ideally from an international organization.

• Hands-on experience with job architecture, job evaluation, salary structures, and compensation.

• Strong knowledge of pay equity and EU Pay Transparency, with the ability to turn requirements into practical processes and governance.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate compensation data into clear insights and recommendations.

• A pragmatic and hands-on approach, with the confidence to advise and challenge HR colleagues and leaders across countries and functions.

• Strong Excel and HR systems understanding, together with fluent English and Danish.

Your Team, Our Culture and Values

You will join our Group HR team, working alongside experienced HR specialists and generalists who work closely together, share ideas, and use each other’s different perspectives and expertise. Even when things are busy, we make room for laughter and a good atmosphere. We value collaboration and openness. For us, it is important that we support one another, and that it is genuinely enjoyable to come to work. Creating and maintaining a positive atmosphere and a great team spirit is something we are all responsible for.

Your leader at ABENA will be Lotte Blanner, HR Director, who describes her leadership style as follows:

“Trust and clear direction. I actively seek and value your input in our shared work, and I listen to your ambitions so I can support both your tasks and your development through honest feedback and clear priorities. I value people who take ownership and show initiative. You can count on me to stand by you and back you up along the way. We aim high but set realistic ambitions and take a pragmatic approach to the realities we work within”

At ABENA, you become part of a global company with a clear purpose: making a real difference in people’s everyday lives. Across the organization, we are guided by three core values: Trust, Fairness, and Cooperation. They shape how we work together, make decisions, and take responsibility for moving ABENA forward.

We look forward to hearing from you and receiving your application.

If you are interested in the position, please send your CV as soon as possible. We review applications as we receive them and will close the search once we have found our new colleague.

Read more about our recruitment process here.

If you would like to know more about the role, feel free to contact HR Director Lotte Blanner at +45 5172 7195.

jobs.occupation: Legal Counsels for Legal & Compliance department at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Legal Counsels for Legal & Compliance department at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you’re energised by varied legal and compliance work and you thrive on supporting some of the world’s largest pharma engineering projects, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for two Legal Counsels to join our Legal & Compliance team in Virum, Denmark. You will join a small, dedicated team of colleagues who daily provides timely, commercially relevant legal and compliance advice that enables our line of business to deliver complex engineering projects.

Your role is key in ensuring that NNE navigates complex legal, contractual, and compliance matters effectively, while supporting our colleagues and projects across Denmark, India, and the US. You will report directly to the General Counsel, who heads the Legal & Compliance team globally.

This is a generalist, hands-on role where your time split roughly equally between legal and compliance work. You will see the practical impact of your advice across the organisation, and you will be given responsibility from the outset, while working alongside experienced colleagues who will support your continued development.

If you are qualified as a Danish attorney (advokat), you can retain your practising certificate in this role.

How you might spend your days

As a Legal Counsel, you’ll be:

• Drafting, reviewing and negotiating consultancy agreements and a wide range of other commercial contracts, including supplier, software, framework and data processing agreements

• Advising projects on contractual matters, change orders and claims

• Driving key elements of our compliance programme across business ethics, data protection, confidentiality and AI governance, including internal audits

• Developing and maintaining legal and compliance policies, standards and procedures

• Delivering training and awareness activities across the business

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Taking ownership from the outset, act proactively and look for solutions.

• Collaborating effectively across projects, disciplines and geographies. You build strong, trust-based relationships with stakeholders across the organisation.

• Delivering high-quality work on time and know how to prioritise when things move quickly. You balance legal requirements, business realities and risk.

• Curious, keen to learn and look for ways to improve how we work. You approach new and complex matters with an open mind and challenge constructively when needed.

• Working independently and in a structured way. Your commercial mindset and genuine interest in NNE’s business enable you to provide pragmatic and legally robust advice.

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• A master’s degree in law (cand.jur.) or business law (cand.merc.jur.) or an equivalent legal qualification

• Around 3-5 years of experience from a law firm and/or an in-house legal function

• A broad legal foundation and an interest in working across different areas of law and compliance

• Excellent written and spoken English

• A responsible, curious approach to AI and new technology.

Life at NNE.

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 22 November 2026.

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact General Counsel Maj-Britt Nedergaard Larsen at +45 30 77 45 63 to arrange a call.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

jobs.occupation: Information Security Consultant at Novo Nordisk Engineering

Information Security Consultant at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you're energised by information security and thrive in a collaborative environment where you can learn from experienced colleagues while helping protect users, devices, and data, we'd love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for an Information Security Consultant to join our Information Security team in Global IT.

As a team, we are working on keeping NNE’s users, devices and data secure — from handling security incidents to strengthening our security platforms and advising the business on security risks.

Your contribution will be important in protecting NNE day to day and in making security a natural part of how our development and service delivery teamwork.

Buying Trainee

Wheat is one of the leading Scandinavian fashion lifestyle brands for children. We are passionate about creating clothing, footwear and accessories that combine timeless design, comfort, and responsible production.

For more than 25 years, we have designed products with great care and attention to detail. Our collections build on a long-standing Danish design tradition, where our most important signatures are high quality and longevity.

We are committed to doing business responsibly — balancing people, planet and profit — and continuously working to reduce our environmental footprint while creating products made to last.

Today, Wheat is powered by an international team of 50+ colleagues with headquarters in our office in Gentofte (Greater Copenhagen), and local offices or showrooms in Munich, Hamburg, Oslo and London.

We believe that diversity of perspectives strengthens creativity, innovation and decision-making — and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels respected, included and able to contribute.

About the role

Have you recently graduated and are you ready to learn buying and product development from the ground up at an international children’s wear brand? We are looking for an analytical and curious trainee to join our Buying & Supply Chain team on a two-year traineeship. We imagine that you come from a programme at EK – Copenhagen Business Academy – or similar.

You will be based at our Head Office in Gentofte, report to our Chief Supply Chain Officer and work closely with Design, Sales and Supply Chain. You will be an active part of the buying team and help build our collections – from planning, costing and negotiation to orders and delivery.

You will have real responsibility from the start, but you will not be on your own. The traineeship is a learning programme where you work on real decisions for our collections with guidance and feedback from experienced colleagues – and your responsibilities grow as your skills do.

Your two-year traineeship

The traineeship bridges the gap between your education and a career in buying. Over two years, you will put what you learned in your studies into practice and gain a solid understanding of the full value chain – from first sketch to finished collection in the hands of our customers.

• 
In the first part of the programme, you will get to know our business, processes and seasonal calendar, and take part in the entire buying process – from collection planning and costing to order placement and follow-up.

• 
As you progress, you will take ownership of a product group or selected suppliers. You will lead the dialogue on prices, quality and lead times, and contribute to decisions on assortment and buying quantities.

• 
Along the way, you will work with our requirements for responsible production, certifications and product safety – and see how they shape our choice of suppliers and materials.

We follow your development closely throughout the programme with regular check-ins, so you know what you have learned and what comes next.

What you will work with

1. Planning & analysis

• 
Learn to analyse sales and sell-through data and use it to plan collections, assortment and buying quantities.

• 
Prepare costings and assess prices, margins and costs together with the team.

• 
Follow the season’s budget and key figures, and point out deviations and opportunities.

2. Suppliers & negotiation

• 
Maintain ongoing dialogue with our suppliers on prices, quality, order confirmations and lead times.

• 
Take part in price negotiations and help assess and develop our supplier base.

• 
Work with certificates, test reports and other documentation as part of our work on responsible production and product safety.

3. Collection & orders

• 
Be involved from collection meetings to finished order, working closely with Design and Sales on assortment and priorities.

• 
Place and manage purchase orders, making sure quantities, prices and data are correct in our systems.

• 
Manage samples and the seasonal timeline, and make sure deadlines are met across teams.

About you

You are curious about the business behind the products and enjoy combining numbers, products and people. You take ownership, keep track of the details without losing the big picture, and want to have a say in what ends up in the collection. We imagine that you:

• 
Have recently graduated – or will soon – from a relevant higher education programme, e.g. Design Technology (ideally with a specialisation in Fashion Management), a Bachelor in Design & Business, or a Bachelor in International Sales & Marketing from EK or similar.

• 
Are analytical and confident with numbers, Excel and costings.

• 
Work in a structured way and take ownership of your tasks from start to finish.

• 
Communicate clearly and confidently in English, both written and spoken. Danish is a plus, but not a requirement.

• 
Enjoy negotiating and thrive in contact with suppliers and colleagues across many countries.

• 
Take initiative and can prioritise between several tasks and deadlines at once.

• 
Are interested in products, fashion and responsible production.

Experience from an internship or student job in buying, fashion or lifestyle is a plus, but not a requirement. We value your motivation, curiosity and willingness to learn.

What we offer

• 
A two-year traineeship with real responsibility in buying and product development at a growing international brand

• 
Guidance and feedback from experienced colleagues who are happy to share their knowledge

• 
Increasing responsibility and influence as your skills develop

• 
Insight into the full value chain – from design and sourcing to sales and delivery

• 
A warm and collaborative work environment where well-being, trust and professional development are priorities

• 
Salary and employment terms that reflect a traineeship position

At Wheat, we believe great work happens when people feel safe, valued and supported. We aim to create an inspiring workplace where professionalism and kindness go hand in hand.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you are excited about the role but don’t meet every single qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

The traineeship is full-time and runs for two years. We hope to welcome our new trainee as soon as possible.

If you are interested, please send your application and CV in English or Danish to job@wheat.dk, marked “Buying Trainee”.

We review applications and hold interviews on an ongoing basis until the right candidate has been found — so don’t wait to apply.

**The Impact You'll Make

**At Danfoss Sensing Solutions, we develop advanced sensing technologies supporting applications across the Danfoss portfolio. As demand for data centre infrastructure, energy-efficient cooling, and environmental monitoring continues to grow, we are expanding our capabilities to develop the next generation of sensing solutions.

As our Senior Mechanical Engineer, you will strengthen our mechanical engineering expertise within R&D and play an important role in developing future sensing platforms, with a particular focus on gas sensing and data centre applications.

You will help transform new ideas into robust, manufacturable products by driving mechanical architecture and packaging development from early concepts through industrialization. You will also provide technical expertise across mechanical design, packaging, and manufacturability while working closely with colleagues across multiple engineering disciplines.

This is an individual contributor role without people management responsibilities. Instead, your impact will come through technical leadership, influencing engineering decisions, sharing best practices, and strengthening our mechanical engineering capabilities.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**You will lead mechanical development activities across innovation and new product development projects, ensuring solutions are technically robust, scalable, and aligned with customer needs.

**Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Leading the mechanical architecture and design of next-generation sensing platforms, including housings, packaging, mounting concepts, and system integration.

• Developing robust encapsulation, sealing, and environmental protection solutions for sensors operating under demanding industrial conditions

• Driving mechanical work packages in innovation and product development projects in close collaboration with sensing specialists, electronics, firmware, manufacturing engineers, product management, and external partners.

• Developing mechanical concepts for gas sensing and data centre applications, including thermal management, fluid interfaces, installation concepts, and system-level solutions.

• Supporting prototyping, design reviews, risk assessments, testing activities, and supplier collaboration to enable successful industrialization.

**What We're Looking For

**You have a strong foundation in mechanical engineering combined with hands-on product development experience. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex mechanical challenges while collaborating across engineering disciplines.

To be successful in this role, we are looking for:

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline.

• Extensive experience developing industrial products from concept through production, including complex mechanical design challenges.

• Hands-on experience with mechanical design of sensors, electronic products, or other highly integrated mechanical systems.

• Strong experience with 3D CAD tools such as Inventor.

• Experience with injection-moulded components and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.

**It Would Be An Advantage If You Also Have

**

• Experience with sensor technology and sensor packaging.

• Knowledge within areas such as sealing and joining technologies, thermal management, tolerance analysis, rapid prototyping, or high-volume manufacturing.

We recognize that great candidates may bring different combinations of experience and expertise. If you believe your background can contribute to developing our next generation of sensing solutions, we encourage you to apply.

**What You'll Get From Us

**You will join a highly skilled R&D environment working on technologies that contribute to safer, more energy-efficient, and more sustainable solutions across a broad range of applications.

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

**Account Executive, SMB (Remote)

**About TrackSights & Your Role

**Every day, thousands of used cars change hands between traders, dealer groups and leasing companies across Europe, and most of those decisions are still made on gut feeling, spreadsheets and phone calls. TrackSights changes that. We turn live market, VIN, government, proprietary and other data into instant, trusted answers on what a car is worth, where it sells fastest and what it will return, so B2B traders, sourcing departments and remarketing teams can price, source and sell with confidence. And with every user we welcome, we're steadily building a network of trusted professional B2B players across Europe's automotive trade, a network our product roadmap is designed to bring closer together.

We started in 2025 and are already used across Europe, backed by Maki.vc and Cox Automotive, one of the world's largest automotive services companies. The product works, users stay and renew, and the sales playbook is proven: the founders have closed every deal themselves. That's exactly the problem worth having. Inbound is arriving, we're welcoming new users from all over Europe, and the founders can't be the whole sales team anymore.

So we're building one. This is the moment where TrackSights goes from founder-led sales to a commercial organisation, and from a Nordic start to the trusted data and insights partner for the used-car trade across Europe. You'd be joining at the start of that, taking over outbound and helping turn traction into real growth.

**What You'll Be Doing

**

• Originate & own deals end-to-end: prospecting, demo, negotiation, close, handover to Customer Success

• Handle SME sales to traders, sourcing and remarketing teams across our ICP in Europe, with no single-country focus, but a strong ICP focus

• Book your own meetings through consistent outbound: phone, LinkedIn, email, sequences in HubSpot and other relevant channels

• Build and manage your own pipeline; your numbers are shared with the team weekly/monthly

• Work with the founders on messaging, ICP and how we sell, and help improve the playbook

• Work closely with our two commercial founders and our Director of Customer Success

**You – You’re a Good Match If

**You're a self-starter and entrepreneurial go-getter who's motivated by growing sales while getting your hands dirty and owning your targets. We're building an organisation of good, kind, smart and ambitious people, with low ego, high ambitions and a can-do attitude.

Relentlessly driven to close. High outbound activity and a constant push to move deals to signature. This is our number one criterion.

• Relentlessly driven on outbound. No one hands you leads here. You build your own pipeline from week one, because without the hard outbound work there are no deals to close.

• Hungry for growth. You want to help build a company with international ambitions, and to grow your own responsibility within TrackSights as you deliver.

• Either 2–4 years in B2B or SaaS sales where you generated your own pipeline (not relying on inbound or SDRs), or a strong network and experience in the automotive B2B field plus sales experience

• A track record of meeting or exceeding sales targets

• Driven to originate your own meetings, not waiting for inbound or SDRs to book them for you

• Builder mindset: you've written your own messaging or sequences before, you test and improve how you sell, and you're comfortable when not everything is defined

• CRM discipline: HubSpot preferred; structured in follow-ups, notes and pipeline, and you use the data to improve

• High ownership and consistency: you don't wait for direction, and you do the work

• You’re ambitious and want your commercial responsibility within TrackSights to grow over time, and take on larger projects or lead a team

**Languages

**

• English (required) and preferably, but not necessarily, Danish: full professional proficiency or native

• Danish, German or Dutch: a strong plus

**Your first 90 days

**

• Days 1–30: learn and get in the game already. Get up to speed on the product, the industry, the ICPs and the sales playbook. Shadow the founders on customer calls and start contributing with outreach and building your own network, already from week one.

• Days 31–60: build pipeline. You’ve already got several meetings in the books and held several. Run your own outbound, book your own meetings, run calls and demos end to end, find your rhythm in HubSpot, and maybe close your first customer. This is ultimately how you learn.

• Days 61–90: own it. Own your pipeline from first touch to close. Your first customers start to close, and you start contributing to how we scale sales.

Clear expectations for activity and results are agreed in writing before you start, and reviewed together every week.

**Why join

**

• Join an amazing team full of good people

• Join a truly exciting growth and international journey together with ambitious people, where only you set the limits

• Real ownership and impact in a company that's building its commercial organisation now

• Work directly with founders who closed current customers and proved the playbook

• Shape how sales is done, rather than executing someone else's playbook

• Where it can go: larger accounts, new markets, strategic responsibility, and in time a leading role with people under you, if you’re up to it. An option, not a requirement

**Compensation And How We Work

**

• Competitive base salary and an uncapped, attractive commission structure, with real upside tied to performance

• Warrant programme, so it feels like your company too

• Fully remote, with the option of an office (to be agreed)

• Danish holiday standards, team offsites (the last one was in Croatia!) and other perks

• High ownership, low bureaucracy, and a strong focus on culture and team fit (we only hire good-hearted people)

**Interested?

**Send us your CV and a short voice note on why this role and TrackSights make sense for you.

We will consider applicants and hire on an ongoing basis, and conduct a structured 3–4-step interview process.

**Your impact begins here

**As Training Partner, you will build the training setup for the future 25L organisation while it is still taking shape. You will identify training needs, partner with leaders and turn business challenges into practical learning that gets people ready for their roles. Your work will support onboarding and capability building as 25L moves towards the PV phase in early 2028 and running production.

**What You’ll Bring

**You bring a strong learning mindset and the ability to translate business needs into practical, impactful training.

• A relevant degree within learning science, psychology, human resources or similar – or experience from a production environment combined with a passion for learning.

• At least 3 years of hands-on experience developing training and learning activities.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships across stakeholders.

• The ability to work independently, take ownership and proactively drive improvements.

• A solid quality mindset and fluent English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**Experience developing training in a structured or regulated environment.

**What You’ll Do

**You will act as an advisor and operational partner to the business, making sure training is effective, compliant and supports performance and continuous improvement.

• Identify training needs and build the future training structure for 25L, including finalising training need analyses (TNAs) with key stakeholders.

• Act as a trusted partner to leaders, showing how training can address business challenges and support onboarding and capability building.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join the 25L Training team in Hillerød, Denmark, where training excellence and continuous improvement are at the core. It is a small team, so you will collaborate closely and support one another in your day-to-day work.

Your closest partners will be leaders, content responsibles and your training colleagues. Together, you will make sure onboarding is effective, capability grows and the training setup can support the business as 25L moves from project phase to running production. Right now, the main focus is finalising TNAs with key stakeholders and building the training setup for the future organisation.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will work close to the business, where your expertise is valued and your ownership makes a visible difference. You will be trusted to take initiative and drive improvements, and supported by a team that helps each other perform. As part of a global healthcare company, you will have opportunities to learn and develop as 25L grows.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from DKK 499,600 to DKK 734,400, corresponding to the level of the position. Placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on your skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to build the training that prepares 25L for what comes next, apply for the Training Partner 25L role by 15 November2026.

For further information about the position, please contact Sr. Manager Steven B. Rødkær, SVVR@novonordisk.com.

jobs.description:
**Job Description

**_Capital planning sits at the heart of how Danske Bank balances financial resilience with sustainable growth. As part of a close-knit analytical team, you will contribute to decisions that enable the bank to serve its customers and support its strategic ambitions. This is a role where your work genuinely matters and where you will build a solid foundation in capital management.

_**What You Will Be Doing

**The Capital Planning team is part of Financial Resource Management in Group Treasury, sitting within Danske Bank's CFO area. The team of seven works on capital target setting, capital issuances, dividend decisions and macroeconomic stress testing. Your analyses and reports will receive close attention from the Executive Leadership Team, the Board of Directors and financial regulators. The atmosphere is collaborative, with knowledge sharing and learning woven into everyday working life, and the team takes pride in delivering high-quality work while enjoying the process.

More specifically, you will:

• Support monthly capital and MREL assessments and projections

• Analyse the effects of regulatory and model changes with relevant teams

• Contribute to stress tests and assessments of capital targets and buffers

• Help analyse payout capacity and capital and MREL funding needs

• Prepare decision material and gradually take ownership of defined deliverables

**About You

**

• Master's degree in economics, finance, business administration or a related field

• Strong analytical skills and a structured, detail-oriented approach

• Ability to communicate complex findings clearly in English

• Curious and collaborative, with an interest in learning and developing within the field

• Comfortable working independently on defined tasks while contributing to team goals

Experience in banking or capital management, and familiarity with Python, SQL or similar tools, would be a welcome addition. We consider candidates at different stages of their career, so we encourage you to apply whether you are just starting out or bring a few years of relevant experience.

**What We Offer You

**You will join a dedicated team where collaboration and continuous learning are part of daily work. We work in a hybrid model, with three to four days per week in the office to support knowledge sharing and team cohesion. You will have room to develop your analytical skills, deepen your understanding of capital management, and take on increasing responsibility over time.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we would be glad to hear from you. Feel free to reach out to hiring manager Henrik Bang at hban@danskebank.dk if you have any questions about the role before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 22 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Are you passionate about bioanalytical operational aspects of clinical trials? Do you have experience within clinical trial planning, timelines, and working with special labs?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new employee in Bioanalytical Operations.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Professional to join our growing team. As a key member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in all bioanalytical operational aspects of clinical trial conduct. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will be joining the Bioanalytical Operational Team in the Clinical Pharmacology & Bioanalysis area, based in our office in Hellerup. We are a well-functioning area, we treat each other with respect, and we never forget to bring a sense of humor to work. You will report directly to Vice President Britta Bysted.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Responsible for all bioanalytical operational aspects of clinical trial conduct on assigned projects according to trial timelines and priorities

• Manage logistics and timelines for execution of bioanalytical sample analysis, from sample collection and processing, shipment, testing, data transfer, including sample tracking, reconciliation, and final sample disposition

• Represent our area in the cross-functional trial teams, working closely with clinical operations, data management, clinical trial supplies among others

• Support bioanalytical outsourcing activities in close collaboration with outsourcing department, including study-specific contract set-up, management of POs and invoices, and relevant communication with vendors

• Provide input, review and approval, where applicable of relevant sections in study-related documents i.e., protocols/ICFs, data transfer specifications, central lab SOWs, laboratory manuals, SOPs, assay performance, bioanalytical reports, etc.

• Contribute to development and continuous improvement of bioanalytical operational processes and supporting documentation

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a bachelor degree in natural science or are trained as a nurse, laboratory technician, or similar with at least 5 years' experience with pharmaceutical drug development. Perhaps you have worked as a sample manager, clinical trial associate, clinical trial manager, or in similar roles.

Furthermore, you have:

• Strong insights into GCP

• Experience with operational aspects of planning and executing clinical trials, and related documentation

• Proven track record in working with external vendors, e.g., special and central laboratories

• Strong IT skills

Key competencies:

• To succeed in this role, we expect you to be able to work independently, be open-minded, flexible, supportive, and detail oriented.

• You are a strong team player with a flair for logistics, and you enjoy being organized and systematic in your daily work. You thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key. You are comfortable navigating cross-functional collaborations and driving alignment among stakeholders.

Travel: 3-7 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Britta Bysted, Vice President of Clinical Pharmacology & Bioanalysis, bvb@ascendispharma.com.

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com
